messages:
Maya G.: FYI spotted recurring p95 spikes when a node thermally throttled last night. thinking: avoid hard evict -> try soft degrade.
Alex R.: where was this? graphs?
Maya G.: dedicated-gpu-prod-us-west-2, ~02:12 UTC. log: `thermal_throttle=true clocks:1100->600 active_tenants=28 p95:620ms->1.8s`
Samir: evict-on-throttle is painful. propose: soft_degrade mode w/ a burst lane + soft-eviction credits for low-priority tenants.
Jin: need concrete knobs. worried about KV cache churn if we evict too often.
Maya G.: rough knobs: on thermal_throttle -> set pool.soft_degrade=true; 1) open token-bucket burst lane for short bursts; 2) apply progressive qps caps by priority; 3) give tenants soft-eviction credits that decay over 10m before hard eviction.
Alex R.: paste a config example?
Maya G.: ```yaml
policy: soft_degrade_on_thermal
burst_lane:
  capacity: 100
  refill_per_sec: 2
qps_by_priority:
  high: null
  low: 5
eviction:
  util_threshold_pct: 90
  soft_credit_ttl: 10m
  hard_evict_after: cost_budget
```
Samir: prefer `hard_evict_after` tied to tenant cost budget not a raw count. also preserve retention for canary models to avoid extra cold-starts.
Jin: routing changes? for soft_degrade we still route but issue tokens slower; add metric `soft_degrade_shed_rate` and alert.
Maya G.: agreed. we'll instrument per-tenant p50/p95, token-bucket drain, kv_cache_hit_after_degrade, eviction_credit_usage. add to pool dashboard.
Alex R.: rollback plan? if p95 for high-priority tenants spikes we should instantly disable soft_degrade flag and fallback traffic to other region/model.
Maya G.: rollout: staging pool `dedicated-thermal-staging` -> prod canary 10% tenants via flag `thermal_soft_degrade_v1`. alert if canary p95 >10% for high priority.
Samir: i'll add metrics: gpu_temp_hist, throttle_events, p95_by_priority, tokens_burned_by_tenant.
Jin: i'll add operator kill-switch and per-tenant opt-out.
deploy-bot: feature-flag `thermal_soft_degrade_v1` toggled ON in staging at 2026-03-22T10:16:00Z
Alex R.: open a short RFC with config, metrics, and rollout steps. i'll review.
Maya G.: will do — thanks, team. this should make thermal events less disruptive without big churn. :thumbsup:
